messages:

Subject: Post-demo: latency window commitments & warm-up timeline

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can lock commitments: 

Summary (short):
- Finvantage target: p95 latency <= 150ms for non-streaming generation at 512-token typical length; p99 <= 400ms is an aspirational target.
- Concurrency target: sustained 1,200 concurrent requests during peak batch windows; occasional spikes to 2,500 for up to 30s.
- Streaming: low-latency chunked streaming required for chat flows (first byte p50 <= 120ms, subsequent chunks <= 60ms).
- Throughput: average token-rate workload ~750k tokens/minute across the fleet during peak.

Key follow-ups we agreed on:
1) Redwood to propose an acceptance run: 48-hour soak + 6 burst scenarios (gradual ramp + sudden 30s spike).
2) We’ll provide a warm-up plan that limits cold starts to <12% of instances at any time; warm pool should cover 40% of expected burst headroom.
3) Instrumentation: Finvantage will share a sample payload mix and 10-minute traffic trace (anonymized) by Monday so we can generate realistic priming.
4) SLA gating: If our p95 goes above 220ms during any validated burst scenario, we gate the rollout and run remediation.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Finvantage (Priya): share anonymized 10-min traffic trace + success/error flags — due Mon 2028-06-04 12:00 PT.
- Redwood (Karthik): deliver warm-pool runbook + recommended warm pool sizing & expected scale-up times — initial draft Tue 2028-06-02 EOD. (attachment: warm_pool_runbook_v1.pdf)
- Redwood (Rishi): schedule acceptance run & share the test matrix/links — Wed 2028-06-03 09:00 PT.

Notes on what we'll test in the acceptance run:
- Cold-start scale-up time (new node boot and ready for traffic): target < 60s measured 95th.
- Warm-pool spin-up: target < 8s from warm-to-ready for traffic.
- Queueing/backpressure behavior: measured tail latencies under overload; ensure rate-limiter penalties are predictable.
- Streaming first byte behavior under concurrency (p50/p95).

I've attached a short CSV with the latency windows we captured from the demo environment (latency-window-profiles.csv) and a first-draft runbook. Please confirm the targets above or flag anything that needs adjusting.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — that summary is exactly what we needed. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) The 1,200 concurrency number is per logical cluster (we operate two clusters in different regions). The 2,500 spike could be cross-cluster but our testing should assume a single-cluster worst case.
2) For streaming: the first-byte target is critical because our UX shows the typing indicator only after the first chunk. If first byte slips over 200ms, we see a noticeable churn in user engagement.
3) Regarding warm pool sizing: 40% sounds reasonable as a starting point but we’d like Redwood to show cost delta vs risk (e.g., 40% vs 25% vs 60%).

I’ll send the anonymized traffic trace by Monday morning. Also looping in Oliver on the acceptance schedule.

— Priya

Hi Priya / Oliver —

Thanks for the clarifications. A few technical details to make the acceptance run deterministic and to help you understand the tradeoffs: 

Warm pool sizing and behavior:
- Proposal: warm pool = 40% of peak headroom (as discussed). We’ll include a cost delta sheet showing 25% / 40% / 60% as requested.
- Warm-to-ready (hot path) expected time: median 3.2s, p95 ~7.6s in our internal staging baseline. We measure this as time from warm instance spin command to ready-for-routing.
- Cold node scale-up (allocate + load model weights): p50 ~28s, p95 ~54s for the model family you saw in the demo (quantized variants).

Queueing and backpressure:
- Redwood routes by policy; when all warm capacity is saturated we apply a short queue (configurable) and then shed to lower-cost fallbacks. For acceptance, we will configure a bounded queue of 120s total capacity per-worker (configurable in runbook) and measure queuing-induced tail latencies.
- Recommended gating: if queuing raises p95 above 220ms for >2 minutes, we mark scenario as failed.

Streaming specifics:
- First-byte for streaming is dominated by model tokenization + network; based on samples we expect first-byte p50 ~95ms p95 ~165ms at 1,200 concurrency unless the path saturates.
- We will instrument chunk sizes and advise a 1-token vs 8-token chunk tradeoff in the runbook; smaller chunk sizes give faster first-byte but slightly more RPCs (cost impact).

Acceptance test matrix (short):
- Baseline soak: 2 hours steady at 80% expected load.
- Spike test A: 30s sudden 2.0x spike from baseline.
- Spike test B: ramp 0%->100% over 90s then hold 5 minutes.
- Burst storm: 6x microbursts (20s) spaced over 30 minutes.

Deliverables:
- Warm pool runbook v1 (attached). Includes exact CLI commands, config knobs, and the cost delta table.
- Test harness links (we’ll drop the load generator URLs in HubSpot and Drive).

I’ve attached the runbook and latency windows CSV used as baseline. If that aligns I’ll schedule the acceptance window Wed morning and provision a temporary warm pool sized per the 40% recommendation.

- Karthik

- p95 non-streaming <= 150ms under steady, p95 <= 220ms during validated bursts; p99 <= 400ms (informational).
- Warm pool target: 40% of peak headroom (Redwood will provide cost delta).

- Streaming first-byte p50 <= 120ms; p95 <= 180ms (measured under 1,200 concurrency config).
- Queueing behavior: bounded queue + deterministic shedding; gate if p95 > 220ms for >2 minutes.

Next steps and owners:

Thanks — looking forward to the acceptance test.
